terms.gloss: a cousin on the father’s side: a father’s brother’s child
terms.grammar: noun, third declension; also an adjective, frāter patruēlis
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.1: L. Cicerō frāter noster cognātiōne patruēlis, amōre germānus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin names a cousin by the parents: patruēlis is the child of two brothers, cōnsōbrīnus, cōnsōbrīna strictly the child of two sisters (Lewis & Short, after the Digest), though it is also used loosely of any first cousin. Traupman glosses cōnsōbrīnus “sister’s son” and patruēlis “brother’s child”, meaning the parent’s sister and brother.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 24, checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 298.
